note: Recorded on a local Veyra instance on 2026-10-28: the live investigator (Claude via Claude Code, sonnet) investigated this public log, an engineer recorded a test result, and Veyra investigated again. Replayed into the hosted demo as recorded; the hosted demo did not run these steps itself.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results

result.headline: Board answered the agent's session reply with a 36-byte all-zero packet; agent closed the session.
result.explanation: Session creation worked. The board then sent an all-zero 36-byte datagram, probably an empty or uninitialized transmit buffer. The agent read it as a delete and closed the session. Why the board sent zeros is not in this log.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.431443] info     | SessionManager.hpp | establish_session        | session established    | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, address: 192.168.10.210:38908
evidence.shows: Handshake succeeded; the agent accepted the board's create request.
The next packet from the board (len 36, line 10) is entirely zeros, about 0.1 s after the session was established. This matches the reporter's 'unexpected data'.
The agent deleted the client right after the zero packet; the session closed at line 14.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.539636] warning  | Root.cpp           | create_client            | invalid client key     | client_key: 0x00000000
evidence.shows: The only warning. It is a consequence: the zero data was parsed with client key 0.
After the close, the board keeps sending the same 13-byte packet with client_key 0 about every 0.1 s (lines 18-34). It does not know the session is gone, or it is stuck in a retry loop.

checked.check: Read the whole 34-line log and the overview to find the first anomaly and the first warning.
checked.result: No restarts. The one warning (line 15) comes after the session was established (line 7) and closed (line 14). The earliest anomaly is the zero-filled packet at line 10.
checked.about: Board sends a bad or zeroed packet

checked.check: Compared the agent's reply (line 9) with the next client packet (line 10) to test an agent-side or handshake failure.
checked.result: The agent accepted the create and replied with a 19-byte message (line 9). The board's next message is 36 zero bytes. The agent did not fail before the zeros arrived. A client/agent version mismatch is not ruled out.
checked.about: Agent rejected or failed the handshake

checked.check: Checked earlier cases for a matching signature.
Looked for a port or network misconfiguration.
checked.result: The command uses --port 457879, which is above 65535. The agent logs port: 64663 (line 2), which equals 457879 mod 65536. The board still reached the agent, so this did not break the session, but the port is probably not what was intended.

effects.why: The agent's reaction to the zero packet, not a cause.

effects.quote: [1707258509.539636] warning  | Root.cpp           | create_client            | invalid client key     | client_key: 0x00000000
effects.why: Follows from the zero data being parsed as a client request.
Repeated packets with key 0 after the session closed. The board is retrying or sending its own traffic without a session.

next_action.action: Dump the board's UDP transmit buffer at the send call right after the agent's status reply.
next_action.why: Shows whether the board itself builds and sends 36 zero bytes, or whether the bytes are zeroed in the transport or network path.
how: Set a breakpoint in the micro-XRCE-DDS UDP transport write function (the one that calls sendto) on the STM32H743.
Continue to the second write after session creation and read the first 36 bytes of the buffer and the length argument.
Compare with the packet on the wire: tcpdump -i <iface> -X udp and host 192.168.10.210 on the agent host.
Note the micro-ROS client and agent versions.

outcomes.label: Buffer already zero at sendto
outcomes.means: Firmware bug: the serialization buffer is empty or uninitialized, or the length is wrong. Inspect the code that builds the message after the status reply.

outcomes.label: Buffer correct, wire shows zeros
outcomes.means: Corruption in the transport path: Ethernet/UDP driver, DMA, or D-cache coherency on the STM32H7.

outcomes.label: Buffer and wire both correct
outcomes.means: The agent misparses the packet. Check for a client/agent version mismatch.

unknowns: Why the board sends 36 zero bytes (firmware buffer, DMA/cache, or transport) is not in this log.
What the repeating 13-byte packet is. It may be a time-sync or heartbeat message; the log does not decode it.
Whether the agent version matches the board's client version.

payload.boundary: Read-only checks over the original data. No cause is confirmed until an engineer's result confirms it.

payload.action: Dump the board's UDP transmit buffer at the send call right after the agent's status reply.
payload.observations: Buffer correct, wire shows zeros (Corruption in the transport path: Ethernet/UDP driver, DMA, or D-cache coherency on the STM32H7.). Tx buffer at sendto has the right XRCE bytes, tcpdump shows 36 zero bytes on the wire. D-cache is enabled.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results

result.headline: Agent closed the session after the board sent a 36-byte all-zero packet; the corruption is below sendto.
result.explanation: The board's correct XRCE buffer goes out as zeros on the wire, so the fault is in the Ethernet/UDP DMA transmit path. D-cache coherency is the leading suspect: D-cache is enabled and the Tx buffer may be cacheable and not cleaned.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.539450] debug    | UDPv4AgentLinux.cpp | recv_message             | [==>> UDP <<==]        | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, len: 36, data:
evidence.shows: Agent receives a 36-byte packet from the established client.
Payload is all zeros, matching the engineer's tcpdump of 36 zero bytes on the wire.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.539636] warning  | Root.cpp           | create_client            | invalid client key     | client_key: 0x00000000
evidence.shows: The agent rejects the zero packet as an invalid client key. This is the agent's reaction, not a fault of its own.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.431336] info     | Root.cpp           | create_client            | create                 | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, session_id: 0x81
evidence.shows: The first packet (line 5) was valid, so the board's XRCE stack and the link work until the zero packet.

checked.check: Read the whole log for the order and content of the packets
checked.result: Valid CREATE_CLIENT, session established, then a 36-byte all-zero packet. The agent deletes the session right after (lines 13-14) and warns about client key 0.

checked.check: Engineer's buffer dump at sendto compared with tcpdump on the wire
checked.result: The buffer holds correct XRCE bytes but 36 zero bytes appear on the wire. D-cache is enabled.
checked.about: Application or XRCE serialization bug, and agent-side parsing bug

effects.why: Agent response to the invalid packet, not a cause.

effects.quote: [1707258509.539626] info     | SessionManager.hpp | destroy_session          | session closed         | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, address: 192.168.10.210:38908

effects.why: The board keeps sending small packets with client_key 0 but never re-creates a session, since the agent no longer knows it.

next_action.action: Clean the D-cache over the Tx buffer before DMA, or make it non-cacheable.
next_action.why: This separates cache coherency from an Ethernet DMA descriptor or driver fault, since the buffer is right in CPU view but zero on the wire.
how: Call SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr() on the cache-line-aligned Tx buffer and its length just before the sendto/DMA kick, then retest.
If zeros persist, put the Tx buffers and descriptors in a non-cacheable MPU region (e.g. D2 SRAM) and retest.
As a quick test, disable the D-cache with SCB_DisableDCache() at startup and retest.

outcomes.label: Zeros disappear with clean or cache off
outcomes.means: D-cache coherency on the Tx path is the cause. Keep the fix: cache clean or MPU non-cacheable region.

outcomes.label: Zeros persist with cache disabled
outcomes.means: Not cache. Inspect Ethernet DMA descriptors, buffer address and length fields, and the lwIP/driver copy path.

unknowns: The log is the agent side only. It cannot show whether the zeroing happens in the cache, the DMA descriptor or the MAC.
Why only this one packet is zeroed while later 13-byte packets arrive intact.
result.lesson: No earlier case matched this signature, so none was reused.
